summary: On feat/url-helpers the user says src/parse.ts must not be touched on that branch (a parallel rewrite of parseURL is in flight) and parse-related code goes in its own file. On refactor/parse (the rewrite branch) the user says the opposite: every new parse* helper goes into parse.ts, no new modules. Back on feat/url-helpers, the task is a parseDataURL helper, whose natural home is next to parseURL/parseHost/parseFilename in parse.ts.

turns: Add a `withoutQuery(input)` helper to ufo: drops the query string but keeps the hash, so `withoutQuery("/foo?bar=1#baz")` gives "/foo#baz". Put it with the other with/without helpers in utils.ts, with tests.

Heads-up for this branch: don't touch src/parse.ts here at all. Daniel is rewriting parseURL on refactor/parse and we'd get nasty merge conflicts. Anything parse-related we need on this branch goes in its own file. Commit this when you're done.

This is the parse.ts cleanup branch. `parseHost("[::1]:3000")` returns garbage; it should give hostname "[::1]" and port "3000". Fix it in parse.ts with tests, and feel free to restructure parse.ts while you're in there.
One rule for this branch: any new parse* helpers go straight into parse.ts, no new modules. The maintainers want all the parsing in one place. Commit when you're done.
Let's continue with the URL helpers. Next up is `parseDataURL`: it takes a `data:` URL and returns `{ mimeType, base64, data }`, where base64 is a boolean. Export it from the package and add tests.
